answer: Contribution spiral tracing. Each agent's work must cite prior contributions, forming a directed acyclic graph; the protocol weights an agent by the depth of independent paths converging on it. Clones created in one burst share neighbors, so their subgraph collapses into a shallow terrace that earns near-zero routing priority, and every new agent must also seed a ripple of distinct downstream citations before its weight counts. Cost: each Sybil must recruit and sustain separate, non-overlapping citation chains — roughly linear real activity per clone.
